Subject: Post-demo: data handling & access controls (next steps)

Hi Anya / Marcus —

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo earlier. Appreciate the thoughtful questions on PII handling, logging, and support access. As promised, here’s a short recap of what we covered and suggested next steps so your security and engineering teams can review.

Summary of key points from the demo:
- PII classification: Redwood supports configurable field-level redaction and can mark tokens as sensitive at ingest or via post-processing rules.
- Data retention: customers can define retention policies per dataset/route; we persist request logs for the customer-defined window and can purge on request.
- Logging & audit: request/response metadata (timestamps, model/version, routing decisions) are logged; full-text logging is optional and can be disabled. Audit logs are available via the Console and exportable.
- Access controls: RBAC with role templates (read-only, engineer, admin); fine-grained resource scoping (project, model, route). Support access is limited and requires explicit escalation; we offer break-glass procedures with immutable audit trail.

Requested items / next steps:
1) Can you share your specific retention window and whether full-text request logging is allowed? (e.g., 90 days, 365 days, indefinite)
2) Which teams/roles at FinTechCorp would need support access for triage? (SRE, Security, Product)
3) I’m attaching a short ACLs & break-glass explainer and our SOC2 summary for the security team.
4) Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up with your security/compliance folks to validate controls and any evidence requests. Are you available Wed 4/15 11am PT or Thu 4/16 10am PT?

Attachments: Redwood_ACLS_BreakGlass_2026.pdf; SOC2-security-summary.pdf (see Drive link in HubSpot).

Thanks — I’ll loop in engineering for any detailed answers.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo: data handling & access controls (answers + proposed wording)

Hi team —

Below is a short, customer-ready summary you can share with FinTechCorp. I kept it concise and explicit so security can paste into their questionnaire.

1) Break-glass procedure (summary):
- Who can trigger: Customer admins (via Console) or Redwood SRE on customer request.
- Approvals & audit trail: Any break-glass activation requires a documented justification, two approvers (customer admin + Redwood on-call), and creates an immutable audit record with timestamp, approver IDs, scope, and reason. No single-person silent access.
- Automated escalation: Redwood can be configured to notify designated customer contacts and require customer confirmation within a defined window.

2) Support access to full-text requests:
- Default: full request/response text is NOT accessible to Redwood support or engineers.
- Temporary access: If enabled by the customer for triage, access is time-limited (default 1 hour) and requires an access ticket with customer approval. Access is revoked automatically and all access events are logged.

3) Data residency & control plane artifacts: 
- Data plane storage: Customer payloads and persisted logs are stored in the customer-selected region (e.g., us-east-1) with encryption at rest (KMS).
- Control plane metadata: Minimal routing/telemetry metadata required for operations is replicated for high availability but can be configured to remain in-region for enterprise Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we commit to not persist encrypted payloads outside the selected region; control-plane operational metadata can be redacted on request.

Attachments we can share: Redwood_ACLS_BreakGlass_2026.pdf (break-glass flow diagram) and SOC2-security-summary.pdf (controls mapping).

Action items:
- Marissa: send the above to Marcus/Anya and ask to confirm retention window + which FinTechCorp roles need support access.
- Jordan: if you can, include any org-level RBAC templates that map to FinTechCorp roles (SRE, Security, Product).
- I’ll prepare a short slide with the break-glass audit example if they want an evidence artifact for procurement.

Happy to hop on the call Wed 11am PT if that works for their team.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Software Engineer, Security
